title: Remove and Refit the Hood Latch Release Handle
introduction:
The hood-release handle sits low beside the driver’s footwell. Its small access cover conceals the retaining-clip opening. I use the main drawing to locate that cover and the inset to understand how the clips release before sliding the handle off its mounting. The socket has a slightly unexpected role here: it releases clips rather than turning a fastener.

This procedure covers the cabin handle and its attachment. It does not teach release-cable replacement or hood-latch adjustment.

items.name: Disable remote start if equipped
items.detail: Before beginning service, disable remote start through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, potentially causing personal injury or death.

items.name: Remove the key
items.detail: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service. An accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Eye and ear protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Gloves for sharp edges
items.detail: Wear protective gloves when handling any components with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.

edits.text: NOTE: The illustration shows LHD (left-hand drive); the procedure is similar for RHD (right-hand drive).
edits.why: Use the drawing to recognize the handle and its retaining arrangement while allowing for the different driving position.

edits.text: NOTE: Insert a 10 mm 1/4 inch drive socket into the opening exposed by removing the access cover to release the clips.
edits.why: The socket presses the retaining clips inward, as shown in the inset. Its job here is to release the attachment, not unscrew it.

edits.text: Remove the hood latch release handle by removing its access cover, releasing the retaining clips and sliding the handle off its mounting, as detailed below.
edits.why: The cover hides the release point. Freeing the clips before moving the handle separates the attachment in the intended order.

edits.text: Remove the small access cover from the hood latch release handle to expose the clip-release opening.
edits.why: The main view highlights the cover at the handle’s pivot area. Removing it gives the socket access to the retainers shown in the inset.

edits.text: Use the socket to press the retaining clips inward, following the inset arrows, until they release the hood latch release handle.
edits.why: The inward arrows identify the retaining action that must be released before the handle can slide off its mounting.

edits.text: Slide the released hood latch release handle off its mounting in the direction shown by the inset arrow.
edits.why: The separate outward arrow shows the handle’s removal movement after the clips have released.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: fit the hood latch release handle back onto its mounting so the retaining clips engage, then reinstall the access cover.
edits.why: Clip engagement restores the handle’s retention; the access cover closes the release opening after the handle is attached.
